## Repaired and pushed - this PR had no live owner, so the CoS took it

Untouched for 21 days. Repaired by a background agent under the orphan-PR rule, adversarially verified by a second agent, then diff-checked and pushed here. New head `e1d4578d`.

## The blocking finding, and what made it worse than it looked

`reopened_after_close()` delegated a **whole-history reduction** to `gh api --paginate --jq`. That filter is applied **per page** and the results concatenated, so the function emitted one verdict per page rather than one verdict.

Measured against api.github.com rather than reasoned about: a 19-event timeline requested at `per_page=2` printed **10 lines, not 1**.

The consequence is the bad kind. A `closed` on one page and the later `reopened` that vetoes it on the next were reduced in isolation - neither page ever saw both halves. The caller's `[[ "$verdict" == "yes" ]]` then compared a multi-line string, failed, fell through to the no-veto branch, and **re-closed an issue a human had deliberately reopened.**

The original finding suggested the sibling `claim_applied_at()`'s `| tail -1` guard as the pattern. It is not the fix here: `tail -1` works for a sibling whose answer lives on the last page, and this logic spans the whole history, so taking the last page's verdict is the same defect with a smaller blast radius. The reduction has to happen once, over everything.

## The gate that should have caught it

The test fixture. The `gh` stub returned a pre-computed `yes`/`no` verdict for any invocation, so it could not express the shape that breaks this - a filter applied twice across a page boundary. A fixture that cannot represent the defect will never fail on it, and that is not a gap in coverage but a gap in what coverage can mean.

## Evidence

Mutation-checked on both halves, each reverted in isolation and restored byte-for-byte against a pre-mutation copy:

- reverting only the reduction back to the per-page `gh --jq` form: both pagination cases red, and the straddling-page case degraded to "its timeline could not be read" instead of "reopened after a prior automated close" - caught by the second assertion, not the first
- reverting only `[[ -n "$raw" ]] || return 2` to `|| return 1`: both unreadable-witness cases red

The `return 2` half matters on its own: an unreadable witness and a witness that says "no veto" were sharing a return value, so a failure to read the timeline was indistinguishable from a timeline that permits the close. Same class as the finding above.

## State

Merge of origin/main was a clean auto-merge (`dd663c2f`); the only files differing from main are `scripts/drain-inbox.sh` and `packages/minspec/tests/drain-reconcile.test.ts`.

**Ordering note for whoever picks this up:** this PR and #2003 both touch `scripts/drain-inbox.sh`, in different functions. They are not independent for merge purposes - whichever lands first, the other needs its branch updated before it can go. The CoS queue holds that order; no merge is being asked for here.

`BEHIND` main and machinery (`scripts/`), so `ready-to-merge` stays red by design and this needs a human `--admin`.

…issues

Root cause: reconcile_done_issues()'s close branch inferred completion from a
merged agent/issue-N branch alone, every cycle, and never removed the
agent-done label it selected on -- asymmetric with the no-merge branch, which
does remove it. A reopened issue therefore still carried agent-done, landed
straight back in the --label agent-done selector on the next cycle, and was
re-closed forever with the identical, over-claiming comment, with no way for a
human's reopen to stick (#897).

- Strip agent-done on the close path too (symmetric with the no-merge branch).
- Add reopened_after_close(): skip closing when the issue's timeline shows a
  reopen after its last close -- a standing human veto on the merged-branch
  inference. Reuses the proven gh api .../timeline REST shape
  claim_applied_at() already relies on, rather than the issue's suggested (and
  here untested) gh issue view --json timelineItems GraphQL field.
- Reword the close comment from a completion claim to an observation, with an
  explicit invitation to reopen.

Added regression coverage in drain-reconcile.test.ts for the label-symmetry
fix and the reopen veto (both the skip and the still-closes-when-never-reopened
case).

re-derivation of "done" from branch-merge state that carried no memory of a

commits.messageBody:
…per page

Root cause: `reopened_after_close` delegated a WHOLE-HISTORY reduction to
`gh api --paginate --jq`, which applies the jq filter to each page separately and
prints one result per page (measured against api.github.com: a 19-event timeline
requested at `per_page=2` printed 10 lines, not 1) — so a `closed` on one page and
the later `reopened` that vetoes it on the next were reduced in isolation, neither
page saw both halves, and the caller's `[[ "$verdict" == "yes" ]]` compared a
multi-line string, fell through to the no-veto branch, and re-closed the very issue
a human had reopened; the gate that should have rejected this never could, because
the test fixture handed the function a pre-computed "yes"/"no" verdict instead of
timeline events, so no test exercised the reduction at all.

The sibling `claim_applied_at` guards its own per-page reduction with `| tail -1`,
which works there because the last page holding a match carries the answer. No such
guard can work here: the answer is not any one page's answer. `--slurp` is not a way
out either — `gh` rejects `--slurp` together with `--jq`.

Fix: fetch the timeline RAW with `--paginate`, flatten the per-page arrays with
`jq -s 'add // []'`, and reduce exactly once — the same shape `approve-on-label.sh`
already relies on against this very endpoint.

The function now returns three outcomes rather than two, because an UNKNOWN verdict
is not a "no" (constitution invariant 2 — a gate fails visibly, never best-effort):
0 veto, 1 no-veto, 2 unknown. The caller refuses to close on 2 and says why, and
`continue` skips that issue only, never the rest of the board. A readable-but-EMPTY
history (`[]`) stays a normal state and still permits the close, so failing closed on
the genuinely unknown does not swallow the ordinary case.

Tests: the `gh` stub now emulates real `--paginate` behaviour (per-page `--jq`,
raw page concatenation without it) and every timeline fixture is real events, since
a fixture that returns the reduced verdict fakes the thing under test. Red before /
green after on the straddling-page veto and on all three unreadable-witness cases;
both halves mutation-checked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
main advanced past this branch when #2047 (fix(#1855): stop reading a
failed lookup as proof of absence) merged, touching the same
`reconcile_done_issues()` function and the same test file this PR
(#1628: stop the reconciler re-closing reopened issues forever)
already changed.

The two fixes are complementary, not competing, and both are kept:
- #2047 guards the FAILED-lookup case: if `gh pr list` errors, skip
  the issue rather than reading the empty result as "nothing merged".
- #1772 guards the SUCCESSFUL-lookup case: once a merged PR is found,
  check the issue's reopen history before re-closing it, and strip
  `agent-done` symmetrically on the close path.

Conflicts were confined to the shared `local` variable declaration
(now `local done_issues n pr veto rc`) and the `stubGh`/`runReconciler`
test-helper signatures, which now carry both PRs' fixture parameters
(`timeline` for the reopen-veto tests, `failKeys` for the
failed-lookup tests).

Root cause of one additional test failure found while verifying the
merge: `stubGh`'s `failKeys` loop (`for f in "$failKeys"`) iterates
once even when `failKeys` is the default empty array, because bash's
`for f in ""` still produces one empty-string word — and that empty
word matched an unmatched call's empty `$key`, exit-4ing every gh
call the case statement doesn't recognise (`issue close`, `issue edit
--remove-label`) whenever a test didn't pass `failKeys`. #2047's own
new tests never caught this because they only assert the call was
*logged* (which happens unconditionally, before the exit), not that
it *succeeded*. Fixed by guarding the comparison with `[[ -n "$f" ...
]]` so an empty failKeys list matches nothing.

Verified: full `npx vitest run` (305 files, 6195 tests) green, plus
`npx tsc --noEmit` and `bash -n scripts/drain-inbox.sh` clean.
